title: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Reference: Packaging, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, Customer Requirements
author: Daniel Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This document is the canonical reference for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It covers supported reference architectures, on‑prem packaging options, a prescriptive VPC deployment checklist, day‑2 operational procedures, and safe upgrade and rollback procedures. It also includes a customer requirements library (network, security, capacity) used by Solutions and Professional Services for scoping projects.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all production Private deployments (VPC, VPC with dedicated subnets, and on‑prem air‑gapped installations).
- Target audience: Platform/Infra engineers, Customer SREs, Solutions Engineers, Professional Services.

Goals and SLOs
---------------
- Availability SLO: 99.95% per customer deployment (monthly).
- Latency SLOs (hosted by private deployment runtime): p95 < 250ms for short-chat gen (<=512 tokens); p95 < 120ms for embeddings calls (small models).
- Recovery objective: mean time to restore (MTTR) for control‑plane issues < 30 minutes with runbook execution.

Supported Platforms & Versions
------------------------------
- Kubernetes: 1.24–1.27 (CNI: Calico, Cilium tested).
- Helm: 3.8+.
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04 / 22.04 for control-plane nodes; RHEL 8.x supported by request.
- GPUs: NVIDIA A10/A100/H100 families supported; driver and CUDA versions listed in packaging notes.
- Storage: CSI‑compatible block storage (AWS EBS, GCE PD, on‑prem NVMe/ceph RBD).

Reference Architectures (High level)
----------------------------------
1) VPC (cloud-managed control plane + customer VPC peering):
   - Components: redwood-control-plane (hosted), redwood-runtime (customer VPC), ingress ALB/NLB, internal service endpoints, optional private link.
   - Network: 3 subnets (control, runtime, management). Public egress via NAT gateway recommended.
   - IAM: least privilege roles for runtime nodes; KMS keys for customer encryption at rest.

2) VPC Dedicated (fully-customer-managed control plane):
   - Components hosted in customer account: control-plane, runtime, metrics, logging stack (ELK/Datadog).
   - Requires VPN or Transit Gateway for connectivity to Redwood verification services.

3) On‑Prem (air‑gapped)
   - Components delivered as OCI image bundle + installer (helm charts, operator).
   - Local KMS/HSM integration (PKCS#11) or offline key import.
   - Optional: an on‑site artifact registry (Harbor) for images and package signing.

Packaging & Installer Options
----------------------------
- Helm charts + values.yaml (recommended for k8s environments).
- Operator-based installs for lifecycle automation (redwood-k8s-operator).
- Air‑gapped bundle: tar.gz with images, manifests, operator binary, and an offline installation guide.

Minimum Resource Profile (per cluster)
------------------------------------
- Control plane nodes: 3 x m5.large (or equivalent) for HA control-plane services.
- Runtime GPU nodes: 1 x GPU node per 8 concurrent gen workers (A100 40GB); scale per workload profiling.
- Minimum disk: 100GB per control node; 1TB per GPU node recommended for model artifacts and KV cache.
- Memory: 64GB per runtime node baseline.

Networking & Security Requirements (customer requirements library)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Outbound endpoints: list of FQDNs (redwood-mgmt.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai) — allow to required hosts or provide proxy.
- Ports: 443 (control plane), 8443 (runtime API internal), 9100 (node exporter), 9090 (Prometheus), 9200 (Elasticsearch) — map per architecture.
- CIDR: customer must reserve /20 for runtime nodes; recommend separate subnets for control/runtime/monitoring.
- TLS: customer must provide wildcard or SAN certs; support for ACME or manual cert upload.
- KMS/HSM: Support for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Vault (Transit), and PKCS#11 HSM integrations. Provide key rotation windows and audit logs requirements.

Example Helm install (VPC runtime)
----------------------------------
1) Add chart repo:
```
helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai
helm repo update
```
2) Basic values.yaml (snippet):
```
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: registry.redwood.ai/runtime
  tag: v2026.03.1
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 2000m
    memory: 8Gi
nodeSelector:
  workload: redwood-runtime
tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Exists"
```
3) Install:
```
helm upgrade --install redwood-runtime redwood/redwood-runtime -f values.yaml --namespace redwood
```

Deployment checklist (VPC)
-------------------------
- Pre-deploy: verify AWS account quotas, VPC CIDR allocation, IAM roles present, KMS policies checked, and NAT/route tables configured.
- Networking: confirm subnets, security groups (443, 8443), and load balancer type (NLB vs ALB) based on model traffic patterns.
- Observability: configure Prometheus scrape targets, forward logs to customer ELK/Datadog, enable tracing hooks.
- Security: upload TLS certs, register KMS key, configure RBAC and service accounts.
- Dry run: helm template to validate manifests.

On‑Prem specific packaging notes
-------------------------------
- Provide an offline install bundle with signed manifests. Bundle includes Helm charts, operator binary, and an "install.sh" which performs image load into local registry, CRD apply, and initial bootstrapping.
- Verify host prerequisites: docker/containerd versions, kernel settings (vm.max_map_count), cgroup v2 compatibility, and GPU drivers (NVIDIA driver >= 525 for H100 recommended).
- Artifact signing: all images are signed with cosign; customers should verify signatures before deploying.

Day‑2 Operations (Runbook summary)
----------------------------------
- Monitoring: dashboards include token-level cost, per-route latency, model health, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
- Common tasks:
  1) Scale runtime: update values.yaml replicaCount or use HPA/CA and roll the helm chart.
  2) Rotate TLS certs: annotate ingress and restart ingress-controller; verify TLS handshake with curl.
  3) Replace failed GPU node: cordon -> drain -> replace instance -> uncordon.
  4) KV cache management: use redwood-mgr CLI: `redwood cache flush --scope <model>` for cache invalidation.
- Runbook for degraded latency:
  - Step 1: Check control-plane and runtime pod statuses (`kubectl get pods -n redwood`).
  - Step 2: Inspect GPU utilization and queue lengths (`kubectl top nodes` / `nvidia-smi`).
  - Step 3: Temporarily increase replicaCount and enable batching limits adjustment per workload.
  - Step 4: If external dependencies (KMS, DB) show errors, follow dependency runbooks.

Upgrade Procedure (Safe path)
----------------------------
Principles: run upgrades as canary -> gradual -> full, with automated health checks and the ability to pause.
Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Backup datastore and etcd snapshots (if control-plane customer-managed).
- Snapshot model artifacts and configuration (helm values).
- Ensure current release notes are reviewed for migration steps.

Canary steps:
1) Deploy new image tag to a single non-primary namespace (or single replica in cluster).
2) Run smoke tests: authentication, sample generation, embedding check, request/response validation.
3) Monitor key signals for 30–60 minutes (error rate, p95 latency, GPU OOMs, CPU steal).
4) If healthy, promote to 30% of traffic via routing policy, monitor 1–2 hours.
5) Full rollout with rolling update (maxUnavailable=1 per control-plane pod, maxSurge=1).

Automated health checks used during upgrade:
- /healthz for control-plane services (200 within 2s).
- Runtime readiness: average 50 successful inference calls within window.
- Telemetry uplink: metrics and logs should show no data gaps > 5m.

Rollback Procedure (If upgrade fails)
------------------------------------
- Immediate steps: pause rollout (kubectl rollout pause deployment/<name> -n redwood).
- Revert image tag in Helm values to previous tag and apply: `helm upgrade --install redwood-runtime redwood/redwood-runtime -f values-prev.yaml`.
- For schema changes: if migration included destructive steps, consult DB migration plan and use backup to restore. Note: Data rollbacks can be costly; when possible implement backward-compatible migrations.
- Validate: run smoke tests and a full regression suite on restored version; monitor for 60–90 minutes before marking as resolved.

Post‑incident & Regression Triage
--------------------------------
- Capture traces for failed requests and record sample prompts that regress quality or latency.
- Create a regression ticket linking to model-onboarding/eval-harness prompts for automated re-eval.

Customer Requirements Library (summary table)
--------------------------------------------
- Network: reserved CIDR (/20), outbound HTTP(S) to 10 FQDNs allowed, NAT gateway, ALB/NLB.
- Compliance: SOC2 / ISO required? (yes/no), if yes enable audit logging and KMS integration.
- Storage: minimum 1TB for models + 30 days of logs at 5GB/day throughput.
- Certificates: wildcard SAN cert or accept upload of PEM chain.
- Support window: Standard (business hours) or Premium (24x7) — define in contract.

Example customer ask: "Can you support air‑gapped on‑prem with HSM?"
- Yes. Deliverables: signed offline bundle, installation engineer onsite or remote, HSM integration runbook, proof-of-concept (2 week engagement).

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (owner: Daniel Chen).
- Escalation: Oncall SRE -> eng-sre lead (pager) -> Head of Platform.
- PS leads for installs: Miguel Alvarez, Sofia Martinez.

Related pages
-------------
- See also: private-deployments-runbook-2026-03-10, private-deployments-vpc-onprem-reference-2026-04-20, private-deployments-vpc-onprem-reference-packaging-day2-ops-2026-03-04.

Appendices
----------
A. Health check endpoints
- /healthz, /ready, /metrics (Prometheus), /version

B. Troubleshooting quick commands
- `kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide`
- `kubectl logs deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood --tail 200`
- `helm history redwood-runtime -n redwood`
- `redwood-mgr status --namespace redwood`

C. Example escalation timeline
- 0–15m: Initial triage by oncall SRE
- 15–60m: Runbook steps executed; if not resolved, PS engagement and customer notification
- 60+ min: Full incident bridge and postmortem if customer impact > 1 hour

If you are preparing a deployment for a customer, use this document as the baseline for your technical design, augment with the customer's requirements matrix, and open a ticket to eng-private-deployments with the proposed values.yaml and network diagram for review.
